blocks.task_summary: Differentiate g(x) = e^(x^2+1) using the chain rule, then evaluate the derivative at x = -1.
method_path: Differentiate g(x) = e^(x^2 + 1) using the chain rule: g'(x) = 2x e^(x^2 + 1)
Substitute x = -1 into g'(x) to obtain g'(-1) = 2(-1) e^((-1)^2 + 1) = -2e^2

evidence.basis: g'(x) = 2x e^(x^2+1) awarded (A2); substitute x = -1 into their derivative (M1); g'(-1) = -2e^2 awarded A1. Total 4 marks.

blocks.task_summary: Find the centre (midpoint of A and B) and radius (half of AB) of a circle given endpoints A(1,4,0) and B(−3,2,−4) of a diameter.
accepted_alternatives: Radius via distance from centre to A or B instead of half of AB: √((−1−1)²+(3−4)²+(−2−0)²) = √9 = 3

evidence.basis: (a)(i): attempt to find midpoint of A and B (M1); centre (−1,3,−2) A1. (a)(ii): attempt to find AB or half of AB or distance between the centre and A (or B) (M1); √(4²+2²+4²) or √(2²+1²+2²) = 3 A1.

blocks.task_summary: Find the exact volume of a right cone with the circle as base and vertex V(−1,−1,0), using V = ⅓πr²h.
accepted_alternatives: Height via √(slant height² − radius²) using slant height from V to A or B

evidence.basis: (b): attempt to find distance between their centre and V (M1); √(0²+4²+2²) OR √(their slant height² − their radius²); √20 = 2√5 (A1); Volume = ⅓π·3²·√20 = 3π√20 = 6π√5 A1.

blocks.task_summary: Show algebraically that ((a^2-1)/(2a))^2 + 1 = ((a^2+1)/(2a))^2 for constant a > 1.
Find the area of the right-angled triangle with sides a, (a^2-1)/(2a), (a^2+1)/(2a) in terms of a.
method_path: Substitute into area formula 1/2 * base * height
accepted_alternatives: Any equivalent expression e.g. (a^3-a)/(4a) or a(a^2-1)/(4a)

evidence.basis: recognise base and height as a and (a^2-1)/(2a) (M1); correct substitution into triangle area formula (A1); Area = 1/2 * a * (a^2-1)/(2a) = (a^2-1)/4 (or equivalent).

blocks.task_summary: Integrate f'(x)=6x/(1+x^2) to get f(x)=3ln(1+x^2)+c, then use (1,5) to find c=5-3ln2.

evidence.basis: Markscheme: M1 integrate, A1 setup, A1 integrate, M1 substitute, A1 final

blocks.task_summary: Find the value of a by using the product of roots and recognising that 3−i is also a root (complex conjugate theorem).
method_path: Recognise 3−i is a root (real coefficients implies conjugate pairs)

evidence.basis: product of roots = 80 (A1)
3−i is a root (A1)
attempt to set up an equation involving the product of their four roots and 80 ± (M1)

blocks.task_summary: Find p using the sum of roots (Vieta) or by expanding the polynomial from its linear factors.
accepted_alternatives: Form and expand factors (z−(3+i))(z−(3−i))(z−2)(z−4) to obtain z⁴ − 12z³ + …, identify p = −12 from the coefficient of z³

evidence.basis: sum of roots = −p (A1)
−p = 3+i + 3−i + 2 + 4 (M1); Note: Accept 3+i + 3−i + 2 + 4 = p for (M1)

blocks.task_summary: Determine P(A ∩ B) when events A and B are independent, given P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.8.
method_path: P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B) for independent events

blocks.task_summary: Determine the minimum possible value of P(A ∩ B), given P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.8.
method_path: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B)

evidence.basis: P(A ∪ B) = 1.1 − P(A ∩ B) (A1); 0 ≤ P(A ∪ B) ≤ 1 (M1); minimum value of P(A ∩ B) is 0.1 A1

blocks.task_summary: Determine the maximum possible value of P(A ∩ B) with justification, given P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.8.

evidence.basis: A is a subset of B (so P(A ∩ B) = P(A)) R1; maximum value of P(A ∩ B) is 0.3 A1; Note: Do not award R0A1.

blocks.task_summary: Show that the implicitly defined curve (x^2+y^2)y^2=4x^2 has no local maximum or minimum points for x>0 by using implicit differentiation, setting dy/dx=0, solving, and applying domain restrictions.
method_path: Implicitly differentiate (x^2+y^2)y^2 = 4x^2 with respect to x using the product rule
Set dy/dx = 0 (condition for local maximum or minimum)
Solve the resulting equation to obtain x = 0 or y^2 = 4, so y = +/-2
Apply domain restrictions x > 0 and -2 < y < 2 to reject all candidate solutions
Conclude there are no stationary points for x > 0, hence no local max/min
accepted_alternatives: EITHER: differentiate (x^2+y^2)y^2 directly using product rule to get (2x+2y(dy/dx))y^2 + (x^2+y^2)*2y(dy/dx) = 8x
OR: expand to x^2 y^2 + y^4 = 4x^2 then differentiate term-by-term to get 2xy^2 + 2x^2 y(dy/dx) + 4y^3(dy/dx) = 8x

evidence.basis: M1: attempt at implicit differentiation, including use of the product rule
A1A1A1: three marks for correct terms in the differentiated equation (EITHER route: (2x+2y(dy/dx))y^2, (x^2+y^2)*2y(dy/dx), and 8x; OR route: 2xy^2+2x^2 y(dy/dx), 4y^3(dy/dx), and 8x)
M1: at a local maximum or minimum point, dy/dx = 0
A1: 2xy^2 = 8x gives x=0 or y^2=4 so y=+/-2. Note: Award A0 for x=0 or y=2 only
R1: since x>0 and -2<y<2 there are no solutions. AG: hence there are no local maximum or minimum points

blocks.task_summary: For f(x) = cos(x - k) with k = π/2 and domain 0 ≤ x ≤ a, find the largest a for which f⁻¹ exists.
method_path: Transform f(x) = cos(x - π/2) to sin(x)
Identify that sin(x) is strictly increasing on [0, π/2] and therefore one-to-one
Conclude a = π/2 is the largest value preserving one-to-one property
accepted_alternatives: Graphical approach via sketching f(x) = sin(x) and applying the horizontal line test.

evidence.basis: a = π/2, A2. Note: For sinusoidal graph through the origin seen with incorrect a, or use of horizontal line test with incorrect a, award A1A0.

blocks.task_summary: For f(x) = cos(x - k) with k = π, find the largest a for which f⁻¹ exists.
method_path: Recognize that -cos(x) is strictly increasing on [0, π]

evidence.basis: a = π, A1.

blocks.task_summary: For f(x) = cos(x - k) with π < k < 2π, find the largest a for which f⁻¹ exists, giving answer in terms of k.
method_path: Compute f'(x) = -sin(x - k) and evaluate sign at x = 0: f'(0) = sin(k) < 0 for k ∈ (π, 2π)
Find first positive x where f'(x) = 0 by solving sin(x - k) = 0, giving x = k - π
Conclude that f is strictly decreasing and one-to-one on [0, k - π], so a = k - π
accepted_alternatives: Sketch the sinusoidal curve shifted right by k, observe it crosses the y-axis decreasing, and the first turning point occurs at x = k - π.

evidence.basis: sketch showing sinusoidal shape decreasing as it crosses the y-axis (below or above the origin) (A1). a = k - π, A1.

blocks.task_summary: Solve the homogeneous DE via substitution y = vx, separation of variables, integration, and initial condition y(1)=2 to obtain y^2 = 4x^2(1 - ln x).
method_path: Substitute y = vx, giving dy/dx = v + x dv/dx
Substitute into DE: (v^2 x^2 - 2x^2)/(v x^2) = v + x dv/dx simplifies to x dv/dx = -2/v
Integrate both sides: v^2/2 = -2 ln|x| + c
Back-substitute v = y/x: y^2/(2x^2) = -2 ln|x| + c
Apply initial condition y(1)=2: 2 = 0 + c so c = 2

evidence.basis: let y = vx implies dy/dx = v + x dv/dx (A1); substitution into DE (M1); simplification to x dv/dx = -2/v (A1); separation integral v dv = -2 integral dx/x (M1); integration v^2/2 = -2 ln x + c (A1); back-substitution y^2/(2x^2) = -2 ln x + c (A1); attempt to substitute x=1, y=2 to find c gives c=2 (M1); final answer y^2 = 4x^2(1 - ln x) (A1).

blocks.task_summary: Set dy/dx = 0 in the DE giving y^2 = 2x^2, hence y = +/- sqrt(2) x and m = +/- sqrt(2).
method_path: Set dy/dx = 0 in the differential equation: (y^2 - 2x^2)/(xy) = 0
Take square roots: y = +/- sqrt(2) x
accepted_alternatives: y = sqrt(2) x and y = -sqrt(2) x
m = sqrt(2), m = -sqrt(2)

evidence.basis: attempt to set dy/dx = 0 in the differential equation (M1); y = sqrt(2) x and y = -sqrt(2) x or m = +/- sqrt(2) (A1).

blocks.task_summary: Find the roots of f(x)=cos^2 x - 3 sin^2 x = 0 for 0 ≤ x ≤ π.
accepted_alternatives: tan^2 x = 1/3 leading to tan x = ±1/sqrt(3)
cos^2 x = 3/4 leading to cos x = ±sqrt(3)/2
sin^2 x = 1/4 leading to sin x = ±1/2
cos 2x = 1/2 leading to 2x = π/3, 5π/3

evidence.basis: valid attempt to reduce equation to one involving one trigonometric function (M1)
correct equation: tan^2 x = 1/3 OR cos^2 x = 3/4 OR sin^2 x = 1/4 OR cos 2x = 1/2 (A1)
tan x = ±1/sqrt(3) OR cos x = ±sqrt(3)/2 OR sin x = ±1/2 OR 2x = π/3, 5π/3 (A1)

blocks.task_summary: (i) Find f'(x). (ii) Hence find the coordinates of points on y=f(x) where f'(x)=0.
accepted_alternatives: f'(x) = -2cos x sin x - 6sin x cos x = -8sin x cos x = -4sin 2x

evidence.basis: attempt to use the chain rule (M1)
f'(x) = -4sin 2x A1
valid attempt to solve their f'(x)=0 (M1)
at least 2 correct x-coordinates: 0, π/2, π (A1)
correct coordinates: (0,1), (π,1), (π/2,-3) A1A1A1

blocks.task_summary: Sketch y = |f(x)|, showing coordinates where f'(x)=0 and where the graph meets the coordinate axes.

evidence.basis: attempt to reflect the negative part of the graph of f in the x-axis (M1)
endpoints have coordinates (0,1), (π,1) A1
smooth maximum at (π/2, 3) A1
sharp points (cusps) at x-intercepts π/6, 5π/6 A1

blocks.task_summary: Hence or otherwise, solve |f(x)| > 1.
accepted_alternatives: Solving -4sin^2 x = -1 leading to tan^2 x = 1
Solving 4cos^2 x - 3 = -1 leading to cos^2 x = 1/2
Solving |2cos 2x - 1| = 1 leading to cos 2x = 0

evidence.basis: considers points of intersection of y = f(x) and y = 1 on graph or algebraically (M1)
tan^2 x = 1 or sin^2 x = 1/2 or cos^2 x = 1/2 or cos 2x = 0 (A1)

blocks.task_summary: Find the total number of possible three-digit codes abc using digits {1,2,3,4,5} with repetition allowed.
method_path: 5 choices for each of 3 positions with repetition allowed

blocks.task_summary: Find the total number of possible three-digit codes abc using digits {1,2,3,4,5} with no repetition.
Given P(x)=x^3+ax^2+bx+c has factor (x^2+3x+2) with a,b,c distinct from {1,2,3,4,5}, find b in terms of a.
method_path: apply factor theorem: P(-1)=0 and P(-2)=0
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 2: Let P(x)=(x^2+3x+2)(x+d), expand to x^3+(d+3)x^2+(3d+2)x+2d, compare coefficients: a=d+3 and b=3d+2, eliminate d to get b=3a-7
METHOD 3: Divide x^3+ax^2+bx+c by x^2+3x+2, set remainder 3a-b-7=0
METHOD 4: Factor x^2+3x+2=(x+1)(x+2), use Vieta with roots -1,-2,p to get b=3a-7

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: (x^2+3x+2)=(x+1)(x+2) A1, factor theorem M1, attempt two equations M1, equations A1, eliminate c M1, b=3a-7 A1
METHOD 2: P(x)=(x^2+3x+2)(x+d) M1, expansion A1, compare coefficients M1, a=d+3 and b=3d+2 A1, eliminate d M1, b=3a-7 A1
METHOD 3: division M1, quotient x+a-3 A1, remainder (3a-b-7)x A1, set to zero M1, b=3a-7 A1
METHOD 4: Vieta A1, roots -1,-2,p M1, sum a-3=p A1, product pairs b=... A1, eliminate p M1, b=3a-7 A1

blocks.task_summary: Show that the only assignment satisfying all conditions is a=4, b=5, c=2.
method_path: use b=3a-7 and c from P(-1)=0 or c=2a-6
test a=1,2,5: b outside {1,...,5} or repeats a
a=3 gives b=2, c=0 (0 not allowed)
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 2: use c=2a-6, argue a=4 is the only possibility from the digit set {1,2,3,4,5}

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: a=1,2,5 lead to invalid values for b R1; a=3 gives b=2, c=0 so not possible R1; so a=4,b=5,c=2 AG
METHOD 2: c=2a-6 R1; correctly argues a=4 is the only possibility R1; so a=4,b=5,c=2 AG

blocks.task_summary: Express P(x)=x^3+4x^2+5x+2 as a product of linear factors.
Sketch y=P(x)=x^3+4x^2+5x+2 showing intercepts with axes.

local maximum point between x=-2 and x=-1
accepted_alternatives: calculus approach using f'(x) to find turning points

blocks.task_summary: Find arg(z0) where z0 = 1 + i, and write an expression for arg(zn) in terms of n for zn = (n^2+n+1)+i, n in N.
accepted_alternatives: For (a)(i): accept arctan(1), pi/4, 45 degrees, or answer marked on an Argand diagram.

evidence.basis: z0 = 1 + i (A1); arg(z0) = arctan(1) = pi/4 = 45 deg (A1); arg(zn) = arctan(1/(n^2+n+1)) (A1); total [3 marks].

blocks.task_summary: Show arctan(a)+arctan(b)=arctan((a+b)/(1-ab)) for a,b in R+, ab<1; then show arg(w1)=arctan(2) where w1=z0*z1.
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 2 for (b)(ii): w1 = (1+i)(3+i) = 2+4i, then arg(w1) = arctan(4/2) = arctan(2), or labelled Argand diagram.

evidence.basis: (b)(i): M1 for compound angle formula for tan; A1 for tan derivation yielding (a+b)/(1-ab); AG.
(b)(ii) METHOD 1: M1 for arg(w1)=arg(z0)+arg(z1); (A1) for arctan(1)+arctan(1/3); A1 for arctan(2). METHOD 2: (M1) for w1=(1+i)(3+i); A1 for 2+4i; A1 for arg(w1)=arctan(2). [5 marks total for (b)].

blocks.task_summary: Prove by mathematical induction that arg(wn) = arctan(n+1) for n in N, where wn = z0*z1*...*zn.
method_path: Base case n=0: arg(w0)=arg(z0)=arctan(1); RHS=arctan(0+1)=arctan(1); LHS=RHS
Apply arctan addition formula with a=k+1, b=1/((k+1)^2+(k+1)+1)
Simplify the rational expression to arctan(k+2)
Conclusion: true for all n in N by mathematical induction

evidence.basis: R1 for base case n=0; M1 for inductive hypothesis; (M1) for arg(w_{k+1})=arg(wk)+arg(z_{k+1}); A1 for substitution of expressions.

M1 for applying arctan addition formula; (A1), A1, A1 for algebraic simplification steps; A1 for arctan(k+2); R1 for induction conclusion. Note: final R1 requires four prior marks awarded. [10 marks].
